payload.rationale:
To resolve as YES, the 2026 annual average must exceed 1.28 C (which also satisfies being above the 2025 value of 1.19 C). The sum of the anomalies for the first eight months of 2026 is 9.79 C, averaging approximately 1.224 C. To reach an annual average above 1.28 C, the remaining four months (September-December) must sum to more than 5.57 C, requiring an average of at least 1.393 C. While the August anomaly reached 1.40 C, sustaining this level over four consecutive months is demanding. 

The strongest reason this estimate could be too high is that the August value of 1.40 C may be a short-term fluctuation, and subsequent months are likely to regress closer to the year-to-date mean of 1.22 C, making the 1.393 C target average out of reach. The strongest reason this estimate could be too low is if the August spike indicates the rapid onset of a strong El Niño or other warming event, which could easily sustain anomalies above 1.40 C through the end of the year.
limitations: The annual target remains unknown, with four months missing.
No ENSO forecast or fitted annual-temperature predictive distribution is supplied.
Assumes simple arithmetic mean of monthly anomalies perfectly matches the reported annual unsmoothed value, which can sometimes have minor weighting differences.
